content: In the United States and Canada, it is advised to contact your doctor for medical advice regarding any side effects you may experience. Precautions: Before starting griseofulvin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This medication may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. Griseofulvin may cause dizziness or reduced alertness. Consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or engaging in activities requiring alertness until you are confident you can do so safely. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages while taking this medication unless your doctor permits it. Drinking alcohol during treatment may lead to a rapid heartbeat and skin flushing. This medication can increase your sensitivity to sunlight. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. Inform your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Pregnancy should be avoided while using griseofulvin, as it may harm an unborn baby. Discuss reliable birth control methods with your doctor while using this medication and for one month after your last dose. If you become pregnant, contact your doctor immediately to discuss the risks and benefits of continuing this medication. The effects of griseofulvin on human sperm are unknown. However, based on animal studies, the manufacturer recommends waiting a period of time after completing treatment before attempting to father a child. It is also unclear if this drug passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not list all possible interactions. Keep a list of all products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Griseofulvin may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control methods such as pills, patches, or rings, potentially leading to pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor or pharmacist whether you should use additional reliable birth control methods while taking this medication. Overdose: If someone overdoses and exhibits severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Laboratory and medical tests (e.g., kidney and liver function, complete blood count) should be conducted while you are taking this medication. Attend all medical and lab appointments as scheduled. Ask your doctor or pharmacist about ways to manage the infection and prevent reinfection, as fungal infections spread easily in warm, moist environments. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This summary does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. For further assistance, contact your healthcare provider or pharmacist.
